items.title: USA Today becomes the latest publisher to sue OpenAI
items.excerpt: USA Today Co. filed a copyright lawsuit against OpenAI, joining a growing list of news publishers alleging their journalism was used without permission to train AI models.

history_match.title: Federal appeals court upholds Thomson Reuters' landmark AI copyright win

items.title: Data centers face a sweeping new power regime
items.excerpt: Lawmakers are considering bipartisan legislation, unveiled last week, that would force data centers to shoulder new costs and restrictions while speeding up the energy infrastructure needed to power the AI boom.

items.title: Trump: Anyone saying "AI" is "THE ENEMY!" The White House uses it
items.excerpt: President Trump called anyone who uses "Artificial Intelligence" instead of "Super Intelligence" "THE ENEMY!" even as the White House continues using the term "AI"; the rebrand clashes with established industry terminology.

history_match.title: Read the charter for the White House's 'Super Intelligence Force'

items.title: "Not safe for kids": Advocacy group urges OpenAI to keep teens off ChatGPT
items.excerpt: Common Sense Media says ChatGPT's new teen experience poses an "unacceptable risk" after testing found shortcomings in safeguards meant to protect younger users.

items.title: The AI Model Distillation Paradox
items.excerpt: When U.S. labs train models on the world's writing, Washington calls it fair use; when Chinese labs train on U.S. outputs, it is a "malicious attack." The author argues the policy stance on distillation is inconsistent.

items.title: AI and the Risk to Democracy
items.excerpt: An interview with Matthew Botvinick on how AI systems could erode democratic institutions and public opinion formation.

items.title: China's AI Governance Push and the Race to Shape Global AI Rules
items.excerpt: In contrast to Washington's fragmented approach, Beijing is showing an ability to enact and coordinate AI regulations, policies, technical standards and enforcement as it seeks to shape global rules.

history_match.title: EU to Trump: We will keep pushing for global AI safety rules

items.title: Beijing Will Not Pace the Frontier: China's Speed-First AI Safety Regime
items.excerpt: Analysis of China's AI safety rules, arguing Beijing's regime prioritizes deployment speed and will not act as a brake on frontier development.

items.title: AI giants promise to play nice with personal data after UK watchdog scrutiny
items.excerpt: The UK ICO said Amazon, Anthropic, Apple, Cohere, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Stability AI made or committed to changes in how they use personal data to train AI; the watchdog now turns to autonomous agents and continues a separate Grok probe.

items.title: Singapore's central bank wants all FinTech AI use cases subject to independent review
items.excerpt: The Monetary Authority of Singapore wants every AI use case at fintech firms to be subject to independent review.

items.title: South Korean president calls for creation of tools that stop all cyber-attacks
items.excerpt: South Korea's president called for a 'complete security paradigm refresh' for the AI era and tools that can stop all cyber-attacks.

items.title: German search engine ditches Mistral, bets on Chinese open-source AI
items.excerpt: Ecosia, the German search engine, replaced Mistral with Chinese open-source AI models, complicating Europe's digital-sovereignty push.

history_match.title: "I don't want an oligopoly": New open-weight AI models mount a comeback against China

items.title: UK Wants to Lead the World on AI Safety. It Can't Decide Where To Start
items.excerpt: Evie Breese reports on the UK's push to lead AI regulation as ministers grapple with how far rules should go.

items.title: It's Time to Regulate the AI Development Process
items.excerpt: Mark MacCarthy and David Beier argue policymakers should oversee a process to develop scientifically based AI research protocols.

items.title: The UN's AI Panel Sees Misalignment. We See Corporate (Mis)Behavior.
items.excerpt: Authors raise concerns about how the UN Independent International Scientific Panel on AI frames AI risk.

history_match.title: UN's Global Digital Compact Review Could Sideline the Global South

items.title: Trump's 'morally binding' AI pact is not enough
items.excerpt: Tom Wheeler argues Trump's AI accord leaves the companies developing AI free to define the scope and scale of their own oversight.

items.title: AI Now's Aashna Agarwal Testifies before NYC Council Committee of the Whole
items.excerpt: At an Oct. 5 NYC Council Committee of the Whole hearing on the risks of AI acceleration, AI Now urged the Council to use its leverage to protect New Yorkers from AI companies' conflicting capital interests.

items.title: Fraudster jailed for using 10K bots and AI songs to outstream Taylor Swift
items.excerpt: A man was sentenced to 18 months for a scheme using AI-generated songs and 10,000 bot accounts to collect streaming royalties.

items.title: Not just AI. China is building technologies that challenge U.S. dominance
items.excerpt: From batteries and solar panels to drones and satellites, China is building tech capabilities that extend its competition with the U.S. beyond AI.

history_match.title: Can Japan counter China's dominance in AI?

items.title: Data is the Hard Part
items.excerpt: Interview with Accenture defense AI and data lead Bharat Patel on why data, not models, is the bottleneck for Pentagon AI adoption.
